questions.q: Where did Yahweh say Ezekiel lived?
questions.a: Yahweh said Ezekiel lived in the midst of a rebellious house.

questions.q: What was Ezekiel to do in the sight of the people of Israel?
questions.a: Ezekiel was to prepare for exile, going out in their sight to another place.

questions.q: How did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to go out?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to dig a hole through the wall and go out through it.

questions.q: According to Yahweh, what was the purpose of Ezekiel’s exile?
questions.a: Yahweh said that Ezekiel’s exile was a sign to the house of Israel.

questions.q: What question was the house of Israel asking Ezekiel as he came out of his house?
questions.a: The house of Israel was asking, “What are you doing?”

questions.q: Who did Ezekiel’s prophetic action concern?
questions.a: Ezekiel’s prophetic action concerned the prince in Jerusalem and all the house of Israel.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would happen to the prince in Jerusalem?
questions.a: Yahweh said that the prince in Jerusalem would go out through the wall, but would be caught and taken to Babylon where he would die without sight.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would happen to the army of the prince in Jerusalem?
questions.a: Yahweh said the army would be scattered, and he would send out a sword after them.

questions.q: What two reasons did Yahweh give for sparing a few men?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would spare a few men so they could record the abominations of Israel, and so they would know that the Lord is Yahweh.

questions.q: How did Yahweh say the the people of the land of Israel would eat and drink?
questions.a: Yahweh said the people would eat their bread with trembling and drink their water while shaking.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would happen to the cities and the land?
questions.a: Yahweh said the cities would be desolate and the land would be a wasteland.

questions.q: What did the people of Israel think about prophetic visions?
questions.a: The people thought that every prophetic vision was prolonged and failed.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say there would no longer be within the house of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh said there would no longer be any false visions or favorable divination within the house of Israel.

questions.q: When did the house of Israel think the prophetic vision of Ezekiel would be fulfilled?
questions.a: The house of Israel had said, “The vision that he sees is for many days from now, and he prophesies of far off times.”

questions.q: What did Yahweh say about the fulfillment of Ezekiel’s vision?
questions.a: Yahweh said his words would no longer be delayed but the word that Yahweh had spoken would be done.

commentary.text: The approaching captivity. (Ezek. 12:1-16) An emblem of the consternation of the Jews. (Ezek. 12:17-20) Answers to the objections of scoffers. (Ezek. 12:21-28)

Ezek. 12:1-16 By the preparation for removal, and his breaking through the wall of his house at evening, as one desirous to escape from the enemy, the prophet signified the conduct and fate of Zedekiah. When God has delivered us, we must glorify him and edify others, by acknowledging our sins. Those who by afflictions are brought to this, are made to know that God is the Lord, and may help to bring others to know him.

Ezek. 12:17-20 The prophet must eat and drink in care and fear, with trembling, that he might express the condition of those in Jerusalem during the siege. When ministers speak of the ruin coming upon sinners, they must speak as those that know the terrors of the Lord. Afflictions are happy ones, however grievous to flesh and blood, that improve us in the knowledge of God.

Ezek. 12:21-28 From that forbearance of God, which should have led them to repent, the Jews hardened themselves in sin. It will not serve for an excuse in speaking evil, to plead that it is a common saying. There is but a step between us and an awful eternity; therefore it concerns us to get ready for a future state. No one will be able to put from himself the evil day, unless by seeking peace with the Lord.
